posts.topic_title: Edwin Land's experiments in color vision
posts.author: Kaveh
posts.post_subject: Edwin Land's experiments in color vision
posts.content_md:
How amazing. I must look at that again. 

OK, it's coming back now. The question is, is this trick showing a new model for color perception, or can it be explained by conventional color theory? Land never made it clear.

There were high level exchanges in the technical journals between Land and Deane B Judd, who is from the conventional school of color perception. My recollection is that Judd was very diplomatic in his criticism (Land was a powerful figure), but one conclusion was that everything in Land's theories could be explained by conventional color theory.

This paper would be interesting:

[http://www.opticsinfobase.org/viewmedia ... 1997&seq=0](http://www.opticsinfobase.org/viewmedia.cfm?id=51997&seq=0)

At first I was thinking that this could be explained by the concept that as you get high energy photons the other colors get stimulated on accident. I believe this is why violet looks like it has some red, there is enough energy to fire of the red receptors and the blue receptors. This is just my assumption. 

However it is quite interesting he was only looking at two shades of yellow!
